rules.title: Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: Landlords are prohibited from terminating a residential tenancy without just cause, which is categorized into at-fault and no-fault just cause reasons.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential rental properties in San Diego with several standard exemptions including units less than 15 years old, certain single-family homes, and government-subsidized affordable housing.
coverage.owner_condition: Exempts certain single-family residences occupied by the landlord or properties where the landlord shares a kitchen/bathroom or owns specific separate dwelling units.

rules.exemptions: Transient/tourist occupancy, short-term rentals, deed-restricted affordable housing, mobilehomes under the Mobilehome Residency Law, hospitals, religious/extended care facilities, dormitories, units sharing kitchen/bathroom with landlord, single-family homes occupied by the landlord renting no more than two bedrooms/ADUs/JADUs, certain owner-occupied duplexes, housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, and certain separately alienable properties owned by natural persons.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.

rules.title: Relocation Assistance for No-Fault Just Cause Terminations
rules.requirement: Landlords terminating a tenancy for no-fault just cause must provide relocation assistance to the tenant equal to two months of actual rent, or three months of actual rent if the tenant is a senior or disabled, provided either through a direct payment or a rent waiver.

coverage.summary: Applies to all tenants subject to the just cause regulations undergoing a no-fault eviction, regardless of income or length of tenancy.
coverage.owner_condition: Applies to properties subject to just cause eviction rules.

rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as the broader residential tenant protections ordinance, including properties less than 15 years old and government-subsidized affordable housing.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord shall, regardless of the tenant’s income or length of tenancy and at the landlord’s option, provide relocation assistance to the tenant by one of the following: (A) The landlord shall provide a direct payment to the tenant... equal to two months of actual rent... If the tenant is a senior or disabled, the direct payment to the tenant shall be in an amount equal to three months of actual rent
